title: Wipe Window
summary: The hovering aerial manipulator holds a yellow sponge in its gripper. Ahead of it hangs a window, a square glass pane in a brown frame, with four small red circular stains on the robot-facing surface of the glass near its centre. Remove all four stains. A stain is removed (it disappears) when, after the first 10 control steps, the sponge's net normal contact force exceeds 1.25 N while the sponge's centre is within 8 cm of the stain's centre.
scene: The ground is the world's z = 0 plane; there is no wall. Ahead of the robot an immovable (kinematic) window panel hangs in the air, facing the robot, roughly at the robot's height: a light-blue translucent glass pane 1.0 x 1.0 m and 1 cm thick in a brown frame of bars 1 cm wide and 5 cm deep; the glass sits at the back of the frame, so its robot-facing surface is recessed 4 cm behind the frame's front face. The glass is slippery (low friction, varying between instances). Four red discs (the stains), 4 cm across and 0.5 mm thick, lie on the robot-facing surface of the glass, each at an independent random spot within a square region about 22 cm across at the pane's centre; they can overlap. The window's distance and sideways offset vary between instances; it is never rotated. The sponge, a yellow block 12 x 4 x 8 cm, is a free rigid body without gravity, placed at every reset between the fingers, centred at the gripper's tool point and aligned with the gripper (12 cm side along the tool's forward axis, 4 cm side across the fingers), with the gripper commanded closed, so the robot starts holding it. Throughout the episode AM-Bench overrides the gripper command with -0.6 on its scale from -1 (closed) to +1 (open): the fingers stay nearly closed and the gripper cannot be opened. Nothing moves by itself. The robot starts hovering level and motionless, facing the window, with its arm at its zero joint configuration (end effector a little ahead of and above the airframe) and the gripper closed on the sponge.
scene_privileged: One environment; its origin is the world origin. Robot at every reset: base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) m with orientation (1, 0, 0, 0) wxyz (body +x is the world +x direction), zero velocity; arm_link1_pitch_joint = arm_link2_pitch_joint = arm_link3_pitch_joint = arm_link4_roll_joint = 0 rad; arm_lfinger_joint = arm_rfinger_joint = 0.001 m (their lower limit: gripper closed, gripper_width 0.002 m). By the robot's URDF kinematics this puts ee_link at about (0.227, 0, 1.124) m with identity orientation and the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + 0.18 m along the ee_link x axis) at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m; the end-effector command is initialised to the current ee_link pose. Window: kinematic rigid body window.usd (gravity disabled), nominal root (2.0, 0.0, 1.0) m, orientation identity; at each reset (Isaac Lab mdp.reset_root_state_uniform) the root becomes (2.0 + dx, 0.0 + dy, 1.0) with dx, dy ~ U(-0.2, 0.2) m independently, orientation unchanged. In the window's frame (world axes): glass box 0.01 (x) x 1.0 (y) x 1.0 (z) m centred at (0.02, 0, 0) (robot-facing surface the plane x = 0.015), colour (0.9, 0.95, 1.0), opacity 0.3; frame bars spanning x -0.025..0.025: vertical 0.01 (y) x 1.02 (z) m at y = +-0.505, horizontal 1.02 (y) x 0.01 (z) m at z = +-0.51, colour (0.4, 0.3, 0.2). The USD physics material (static 0.6, dynamic 0.5, restitution 0.1) is overridden at each reset by mdp.randomize_rigid_body_material on all window shapes: static friction ~ U(0.2, 0.4), dynamic ~ U(0.1, 0.3) (kept <= static), restitution 0, from 16 buckets sampled at startup. Stains: kinematic bodies Dot_0..Dot_3 (gravity disabled, collision enabled), cylinders radius 0.02 m, thickness 0.0005 m, axis along the window's x, colour (0.8, 0.2, 0.2). At each reset, after the window, dot i is placed at window_root + (0.015, y_i, z_i) (centred on the glass surface) with y_i, z_i ~ U(-0.09, 0.09) m, all draws independent (no overlap check), orientation the window's; AM-Bench's stain_pos observation is these centres. A removed stain is only hidden (USD visibility off); its collider stays. All stains are made visible again at reset. Sponge: dynamic cuboid 0.12 (x) x 0.04 (y) x 0.08 (z) m, mass 0.05 kg, gravity disabled, contact offset 0.005 m, colour (0.95, 0.75, 0.3), scene default physics material (friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0), with an Isaac Lab ContactSensor. At each reset, after the robot, the sponge is placed at the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + R(ee_link) (0.18, 0, 0)) with the ee_link orientation and zero velocity: centre at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m, axes along the world axes. The gripper target is set to closed (-1); the FA-Hexa defines no object-width converter, so the finger joints are not preset to the sponge's 0.04 m. In every step AM-Bench sets the gripper action (the last action component) to -0.6 before processing it: per-finger target 0.001 + 0.2 x (0.045 - 0.001) = 0.0098 m (gripper width 0.0196 m), whatever the agent sends. None of the task's own assets (window, stains, sponge) reference the web.
success: Success at the first control step after which all four stains have been removed. Stain removal is updated at the start of every control step (before its physics step, on the state reached at the end of the previous step) and is disabled while episode_length_buf < 10 (the first 10 steps). Stain i is removed at an update where all hold: (1) the magnitude of the sponge's net normal contact force (ContactSensor net_forces_w: the vector sum of the normal forces of all its contacts, glass, frame, stains, gripper fingers or anything else; the sensor's window filter is not used) is > 1.25 N (stain_removal_force_threshold); (2) the distance from the sponge's centre (its root position) to stain i's centre is <= 0.08 m (stain_removal_contact_radius); (3) stain i is still visible. One contact event suffices (stain_removal_contact_count = 1, counted on rising edges), so a stain goes at the first update where this holds; several can go at once, and removed stains stay removed until reset. AM-Bench reports stain_0_removed .. stain_3_removed as subtask criteria; they are informational only. The all-removed test runs after every control step (decimation 1, 1/120 s); no hold time is required, and the episode terminates at the step in which the last stain was removed. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 20 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 2400 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 2399th step.
difficulty_note: Four separate small stains each need a firm press (net contact force above 1.25 N) with the sponge's centre close to them, on slippery glass, with a sponge held only by the fingers' grip on a hovering base; the stain layout and the window's position change per instance.
standard_notes: Neither the stain positions, nor which stains remain, nor the contact force is given: the window and the stains have to be located with the onboard cameras (the held sponge occupies part of the end-effector camera's view) and related to the robot through proprioception (base and end-effector poses). A removed stain disappears from the images. The gripper command has no effect in this task.
